faqs.q: Sec. 14-207. - Disposition of animal after acquittal or conviction.
faqs.a:
(a)
Acquittal.
Should the owner or custodian of an impounded animal be acquitted of all charges
               relating to the impoundment of the animal, the court will order the animal returned
               to the owner or custodian and shall order the city and the animal shelter to refund
               to the owner or custodian all payments made for the impoundment, care, and provision
               for the animal as appropriate.
Exception:
Notwithstanding the above, the owner or custodian remains responsible for the payment
               of costs for veterinary care reasonably necessary to assess and stabilize the animal
               and to otherwise provide reasonable veterinary care to the animal throughout the term
               of its impoundment.
(b)
Conviction; authority to order forfeiture.
In addition to the sentencing authority of a municipal court judge otherwise set
               forth in this Code, a municipal court judge may order the forfeiture of an animal
               or animals as part of the sentence following a conviction for violating any of the
               following charges in this chapter:
(1)
Section 14-51
, dangerous animals;
(2)
Section 14-52
, aggressive animals;
(3)
Section 14-54
, running at large;
(4)
Section 14-91
, certain animals prohibited;
(5)
Section 14-171
, cruelty;
(6)
Section 14-171.5
, neglect;
(7)
Section 14-174
, care of animals; or
(8)
Following a conviction of any charge set forth in this chapter of a person who is
               or has been adjudged a habitual offender under
section 14-11
of this chapter.
(c)
Considerations.
In determining whether an animal should be forfeited following a conviction for a
               violation listed in subsection (b) of this section, a municipal court judge may consider
               the following factors in relation to the health and safety of the community and the
               animal involved:
(1)
Nature and severity of an attack.
Whether the animal attacked a person or another animal, and the nature and severity
               of that attack;
(2)
Behavioral circumstances.
The existence of any provocation or other extenuating circumstances relevant to the
               animal's behavior;
(3)
Corrective measures.
The apparent ability of the owner to properly care for the animal including corrective
               measures taken to lessen the chances of a future violation of this chapter;
(4)
History of animal.
Whether the animal has been involved in other incidents, including incidents of the
               animal running at large;
(5)
History of owner.
Past allegations of improper care involving the animal, owner, or custodian;
(6)
Expert evaluations.
Any expert evaluation relating to the animal or the owner's or custodian's care,
               treatment, or disposition of the animal; and
(7)
Other.
Any other factor the court determines is relevant to the health and safety of the
               community or animal.
(d)
Contents of order.
(1)
Forfeiture appropriate.
Should a municipal court judge determine that forfeiture of the animal is appropriate,
               the judge will order the animal be deemed the property of the animal shelter and order
               the owner or custodian of any animal not already in the custody of the shelter to
               release the forfeited animal to an animal management officer for impoundment. The
               judge may also order that the animal be destroyed, but may stay this portion of the
               order if, within seven days of the court's forfeiture order, the owner or custodian
               asks the court to stay the destruction order until the date for the filing of an appeal
               of the municipal court case has passed.
(i)
If the judge orders an animal to be destroyed, the judge will order that the animal
               owner or custodian pay all costs arising from the impoundment, care of, and provision
               for the animal through the time it is destroyed.
(2)
Forfeiture not appropriate.
Should a municipal court judge determine that forfeiture of the animal is not appropriate
               under this section, the judge may issue any order related to the release, care of,
               or provision for the animal that the judge deems appropriate to the circumstances.
               In each case, the judge will order that the animal owner or custodian pay all costs
               arising from the impoundment, care of, and provision for the animal through the time
               it is released or otherwise disposed of.
(e)
Production of forfeited animal; failure to produce.
The animal owner or custodian of any animal not already in the custody of the animal
               shelter that is subject to a forfeiture order must produce the forfeited animal to
               an animal management officer within 24 hours of the court's forfeiture order. The
               court may exercise its powers of contempt should the owner or custodian fail to produce
               the animal as ordered.
(
Ord. No. 4878
, § 9, 10-7-2024)
